goal: Create and genuinely test ORBIT-360, a documented ACFV-reference-scale project that materializes 360 dependency-aware units with bounded execution, resume, and affected-closure repair.
acceptance_criteria: A real CLI run materializes all unit files, validates their hashes and dependencies, executes all units, and writes an inspectable run report.
Resume skips verified completed units, while repair of one unit recalculates only its transitive downstream closure.
The benchmark accepts no arbitrary command or generated code execution and labels its reports as support evidence rather than formal delivery PASS.
The default plan contains exactly 360 deterministic work units arranged in dependency layers of width 35.
The project includes a Chinese project vision and a copy-paste usage guide that explain how it differs from and matches the ACFV reference scale.
Unit and end-to-end tests pass against a real 360-unit workspace within a bounded local runtime.

quality_metrics.measure: formal provider and delivery route preservation
quality_metrics.target: kernel and provider contract tests pass without a new generation or delivery path
quality_metrics.method: existing kernel and formal provider test profiles

quality_metrics.measure: bounded context and affected-work repair at increasing project scale
quality_metrics.target: context remains within configured budgets and unrelated checkpoints remain reusable
quality_metrics.method: generation scale ladder and ACFV-scale trial

prevention: Confirm acceptance, interfaces, and applicable kernel constraints before implementation.
assurance: Review method, schema, skill, and repository instruction consistency.
Validate that support artifacts cannot authorize formal delivery PASS.
Review changed files against the kernel contract before integration.
control: Run targeted kernel and knowledge tests.
improvement: Record review findings and one bounded improvement experiment.

feedback: ORBIT-360 meets the bounded ACFV-reference-scale acceptance criteria without adding a generation or delivery path.

worked: Compact source plus deterministic runtime materialization kept the repository reviewable while genuinely exercising 360 dependency-aware units.
did_not_work: The first semantic-tamper assertion expected downstream recomputation even though deterministic root recovery restored the original dependency hash; the assertion was corrected to the true minimal-recompute behavior.
experiments: Reuse a fully valid checkpoint, alter one target, and measure whether exactly the 11-unit transitive closure is recomputed while 349 units remain reusable.
